headline: BenchShield models agent-evaluation reward integrity across the full task lifecycle
summary: A September 10 arXiv paper presents BenchShield, which models reward-relevant events in interactive agent benchmarks and combines static phase-aware taint analysis with runtime evidence from the evaluation infrastructure. The authors report a corpus of 456 human-adjudicated trajectories selected from more than 31,000 public runs across Terminal-Bench 3, SkillsBench and ClawsBench. On paired, author-selected task audits, reported full-chain exploit recall rises over an agentic scanner baseline in all three benchmark sets (for example, 0.77 vs 0.23 on Terminal-Bench 3 and 1.00 vs 0.94 on ClawsBench, union over five trials). Runtime attribution reports 96% accuracy among covered cases in 144 runnable cells, with 87.5% coverage and inconclusive verdicts for the rest. Results are author-reported and do not establish general benchmark prevalence, complete exploit prevention or transfer to unrelated environments.
